## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Devadatta Sutta* (Iti 89; It 3.40, PTS It 85) is a short discourse preserved in the *Tikanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The sutta addresses the spiritual ruin of the Buddha's schismatic cousin, declaring that Devadatta, having been conquered and overwhelmed by three forms of unwholesome qualities or false teachings (*asaddhamma*), was incurably doomed to a state of deprivation and perdition [SuttaCentral].
Echoing accounts found in the Vinaya, the discourse contains verse lines describing Devadatta when he was still regarded as an accomplished ascetic—a sage of developed mind (*bhavit’atta*) who shone brightly with fame [Piya Tan 2002, 2004]. In explaining this verse, the *Itivuttaka* commentary (*Paramatthadīpanī*, ItA 2:100) clarifies that *bhavit’atta* does not denote the transcendent development of the noble path, but rather indicates that Devadatta's mind was developed through the mundane higher knowledges and meditative absorptions (*jhānâbhiññāhi bhāvitacitto*) prior to his downfall [Piya Tan 2002, 2004].
The text is closely intertwined with the Vinaya narrative of the schism: SuttaCentral records passage-level parallels in the *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* of the Khandhaka (Kd 17), the *Ekuttarikanaya* of the *Parivāra* (Pvr 7), and various recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 14 / UVS 14 / Uv Kg 14; Chinese T 212.15 and T 213.14) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly corroborates this reuse, detecting extensive Pali-internal text sharing between Iti 89 (§2.4–9.4) and Kd 17 (§4.7.49–5.1.0), as well as significant correspondences with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 8, AN 6, AN 3) and fellow *Itivuttaka* discourses (Iti 59, Iti 86, Iti 92) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignment, DharmaNexus finds high textual matches with the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* (SA K01 vinv172u), as well as connections with the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125, fascicle 48), the Chinese *Saṁyukta Āgama* (T 99), and the Tibetan *Ārya-mañjuśrīmūlatantra* (D0543) [DharmaNexus].
